title: Animals, Food and Food Chains
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Animals, Food and Food Chains Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Animals get food in different ways; food chains show how energy passes from producers (plants) to consumers and decomposers. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 4, Quarter 2: Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Living Things): producers, consumers, decomposers, food chains, food webs, changes in a food web and energy and the Sun. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy flows from the Sun to plants to animals.
key_sub: Producers make food; consumers eat; decomposers break down dead things.
body_html:
How to think about it

A food chain shows who eats whom. The arrows point from the food to the eater.

  • Producers (plants and algae) make their own food using sunlight.
  • Consumers eat other living things: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.
  • Decomposers (fungi, bacteria, worms) break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.
  • A food web is many linked food chains. If one population changes, others change too.
Example

Grass → hare → lynx. Which is the producer?

the grass makes its own food

Answer: grass

Example

If the hares disappear, what happens to the lynx?

lynx eat hares

less food

Answer: the lynx population falls

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the arrows backwards (the arrow points to the eater).
  • Thinking decomposers are not important.
  • Thinking a change to one animal affects only that animal.

faq.q: Why do food chains start with a plant?
faq.a: Plants are producers. They capture energy from the Sun and make food, so all the energy in the chain starts with them.

faq.q: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
faq.a: A food chain is one path of energy. A food web shows many food chains linked together.
They break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil so new plants can grow.

items.q: Is a bracket fungus a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Food chain: lettuce → slug → shrew → civet. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Food chain: seaweed → periwinkle → crab → herring gull. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Is a slater a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Is wattle a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Producers make their own food from sunlight.

items.q: What is a food web?
c: many food chains that are linked together
items.e: Most animals eat more than one thing.

items.q: Seagrass grows in shallow sea water. What is its role?
c: a producer that feeds dugongs and turtles
items.e: Seagrass makes food from sunlight.

items.q: In a pond: algae → tadpole → fish → heron. Which is the top consumer?
items.e: The heron is at the end of the chain.

items.q: Why are there usually fewer wolves than Philippine deer in a forest?
c: Energy is lost at each step, so there is less energy for animals higher up the chain.
items.e: Each level supports fewer animals.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: Food chain: lettuce → slug → shrew → civet. What eats the slug in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. What eats the mayfly larva in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Is banksia a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Producers make their own food from sunlight.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Food chain: grain → field vole → kestrel. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: Pond food web: algae and duckweed are eaten by tadpoles and snails. Fish eat tadpoles. Herons eat fish and frogs. Which living things are producers?
items.e: Producers are the plants and algae.

items.q: What is prey?
c: an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
items.e: Mice are prey for owls.

items.q: Earthworms eat dead leaves. What role do they play?
items.e: Worms help recycle nutrients.

items.q: Which is a scavenger that eats dead animals?
items.e: Scavengers clean up dead animals.

items.q: Lake food chain: algae → zooplankton → minnow → walleye. What does the minnow eat?
items.e: Follow the arrow into the minnow.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: aphid, blackbird, ladybug, nettles?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
c: heron → algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly → frog
algae → mosquito larva → turtle → frog → heron
algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly → frog → heron
heron → frog → dragonfly → mosquito larva → algae
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: algae → mosquito larva → dragonfly → frog → heron.

items.q: Lake food chain: algae → zooplankton → minnow → walleye → osprey. What eats the walleye?
items.e: The arrow from walleye points to the osprey.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: heron, pondweed, tadpole, water beetle?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: acorns, tawny owl, wood mouse?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.e: Nutrients help new plants grow.

items.e: Bacteria recycle nutrients.

items.q: Where does the energy in almost every food chain come from first?
items.e: Plants use the Sun's energy to make food.

items.q: This is an ocean food web. How many kinds of food does the orca eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the orca: seal, sea otter.

items.q: This is a pond food web. What does the mosquito larva eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the algae to the mosquito larva, so the mosquito larva eats algae.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Which of these is food for the heron?
items.e: The arrow goes from the frog to the heron, so the heron eats a frog.

items.q: This is a pond food web. Which animal eats the mosquito larva?
items.e: An arrow goes from the mosquito larva to the small fish.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Which animal eats the snail?
items.e: An arrow goes from the snail to the turtle.

items.q: This is a coral reef food web. In this web, the parrotfish's food is: seaweed. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only plants (producers).

items.q: A wolf eats Philippine deer. A Philippine deer eats grass. What is the Philippine deer?
items.e: Deer eat only plants.

items.q: Use the forest food web. Which animal eats the squirrel?
items.e: An arrow goes from the squirrel to the owl.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Which animal eats the pondweed?
items.e: An arrow goes from the pondweed to the turtle.

items.q: Use the forest food web. In this web, the robin's food is: caterpillar, berry bush. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats both plants and animals.

items.q: Use the forest food web. Which animal eats the robin?
items.e: An arrow goes from the robin to the owl.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Which of these is food for the guppy?
items.e: The arrow goes from the mosquito larva to the guppy, so the guppy eats a mosquito larva.

items.q: This is a coral reef food web. What does the squid eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the small fish to the squid, so the squid eats a small fish.

items.q: Look at the school garden food web. How many kinds of food does the garden lizard eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the garden lizard: spider, grasshopper.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. In this web, the shark's food is: squid, parrotfish. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. Which of these is food for the civet?
items.e: The arrow goes from the rabbit to the civet, so the civet eats a rabbit.

items.q: This is a pond food web. In this web, the mosquito larva's food is: algae. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only plants (producers).

items.q: This is a pond food web. How many kinds of food does the heron eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the heron: frog, guppy.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. If all the caterpillars were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer oak leaves.
There would probably be more oak leaves.
items.e: With no caterpillars eating them, more oak leaves survive.

items.q: This is a coral reef food web. Most of the small fish are removed from the coral reef. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the small fish eats zooplankton. With fewer predators, more zooplankton survive.

items.q: Which living thing is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead things.

items.q: Food chain: grain → field vole → kestrel. If all the field voles were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer grain.
There would probably be more grain.
items.e: With no field voles eating them, more grain survive.

items.q: Meadow food chain: clover → grasshopper → garter snake → red-tailed hawk. Which is a carnivore that is also eaten?
items.e: The snake eats grasshoppers and is eaten by hawks.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. If the number of dandelions fell, what would most likely happen to the snails?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Use the forest food web. A disease kills most of the Philippine deer. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The wolf eats only Philippine deer. Without them, the wolf has little food.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Most of the herons are removed from the pond. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the heron eats small fish. With fewer predators, more small fish survive.

items.q: What does an arrow in a food chain show?
c: the direction energy moves when one thing is eaten
items.e: The arrow points to the eater.

items.q: Food chain: acorns → wood mouse → tawny owl. If the number of acorns fell, what would most likely happen to the wood mice?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. A disease kills most of the small fish. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The coral trout eats only small fish. Without them, the coral trout has little food.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. If all the trout were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be more mayfly larvae.
There would probably be fewer mayfly larvae.
items.e: With no trout eating them, more mayfly larvae survive.

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. If the number of water beetles fell, what would most likely happen to the herons?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Use the ocean food web. A disease kills most of the phytoplankton. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The krill eats only phytoplankton. Without them, the krill has little food.

items.q: Use the forest food web. Most of the owls are removed from the forest. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the owl eats squirrel. With fewer predators, more squirrel survive.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. If all the cats were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer song thrushes.
There would probably be more song thrushes.
items.e: With no cats eating them, more song thrushes survive.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. A disease kills most of the algae. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The mosquito larva eats only algae. Without them, the mosquito larva has little food.

items.q: Use the pond food web. A disease kills most of the mosquito larvae. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The dragonfly nymph eats only mosquito larvae. Without them, the dragonfly nymph has little food.

items.q: Use the school garden food web. Most of the snakes are removed from the school garden. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the snake eats garden lizards. With fewer predators, more garden lizards survive.

items.q: A farmer sprays a field to kill all the grasshoppers. What might happen to the frogs that eat them?
c: The frogs have less food and their number may fall.
items.e: Changes travel through food webs.

items.q: What does a food chain show?
c: what eats what, and how energy passes from one living thing to another
items.e: Arrows show energy flow.

items.q: Wolves were brought back to a park where Philippine deer had eaten most young trees. Later, more young trees grew. Why?
c: Wolves ate some Philippine deer, so fewer Philippine deer ate the trees.
items.e: A change at the top of a food web can spread down to the plants.

items.q: Which change would affect the most organisms in a food web?
items.e: Every food chain begins with producers, so all consumers depend on them.

items.q: What do we call an animal that hunts and eats other animals?
items.e: The animal that is eaten is the prey. The hunter is the predator.

items.q: Which organisms break down dead plants and animals?
c: decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria
items.e: Decomposers return matter from dead organisms to the soil.

items.q: Can an animal be both predator and prey?
c: Yes, for example a blue tit eats caterpillars but is eaten by sparrowhawks.
items.e: Middle of the chain.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. The energy in the frog's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the frog.

items.q: A herbivore eats
items.e: Rabbits and Philippine deer are herbivores.

items.q: In a food chain, what does an arrow show?
c: that the first organism eats the second
the direction food energy and matter move, from the food to the eater
items.e: An arrow from grass to rabbit means the rabbit eats the grass; matter and energy move to the rabbit.

items.q: What is a consumer?
c: an organism that gets energy by eating other organisms
a plant that makes its own food
items.e: Animals are consumers. They cannot make their own food.

items.q: What is a producer?
c: a living thing that breaks down dead matter
an animal that eats other animals
an organism that makes its own food, like a plant
items.e: Producers, such as plants and algae, use sunlight to make their own food.

items.q: Use the school garden food web. The energy in the mynah's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the mynah.

items.q: What is a top predator?
c: the first living thing in a chain
an animal at the end of a food chain that nothing in the chain eats
items.e: Such as an owl or a civet.

items.q: This is a pond food web. The energy in the small fish's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the small fish.

items.q: The number of mosquitoes in a pond fell after guppies were added. Why?
c: Guppies eat adult mosquitoes in the air.
items.e: Guppies are used to control mosquito breeding.

items.q: A graph shows that when the number of snakes in a garden fell, the number of mynahs rose. What is the best explanation?
c: Fewer mynahs were eaten by snakes.
items.e: Fewer predators means more prey survive.

items.q: A farmer sprays a field to kill all the insects. Which effect is most likely?
c: Birds that eat insects have less food.
items.e: Removing one population affects the animals that eat it.

items.q: Which way do the arrows in a food chain point?
c: from the eater to its food
from the food to the animal that eats it
items.e: Read arrows as 'is eaten by'.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. The energy in the mouse's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the mouse.

items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the turtle.
